rounds.text: Borosil Ltd is demonstrably mispriced because its underlying business fundamentals have compounded at a faster rate than the stock price over a five-year period [E46]. Specifically, compounded sales growth has reached a robust 16% over the same five years [E8]. Furthermore, structural profitability has structurally expanded, with operating margins rising to 14% by March 2026 compared to just 9% three years prior, marking an impressive improvement of 5 percentage points [E20]. Because profit growth of 14% has outpaced the 6% stock price increase over five years, the fundamental engine is clearly pulling ahead of market valuation [E46]. conceded: [E35], [E37], [E59]

The valuation disconnect is stark, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 190 per share against a market price of Rs 244 [E35], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -28.4% [E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF reveals that today's price aggressively prices in 17.4% earnings growth, which outpaces the 14.0% growth assumed in the base case [E37]. This lofty valuation of 37.8x P/E [E1] and 3.29x price-to-book [E2] rests on mediocre underlying profitability, evidenced by an ROE of just 9.2% [E7] and a modest ROCE of 11.5% [E6]. Operational headwinds are already materialising as quarterly operating margins have contracted to 11% in March 2026 compared to 14% in the year-ago quarter [E21], while the stock offers zero dividend support at a 0.00% yield [E4]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is 16% [E8], and profit growth has outpaced the stock price over the same period [E46].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 190 against a market price of Rs 244, yielding a negative margin of safety of -28.4% [E35, E36], and quarterly operating margins compressed to 11% in March 2026 from 14% a year prior [E21]. However, the bear ignores the broader structural margin expansion over a multi-year horizon, where operating margins climbed to 14% in March 2026 from just 9% three years earlier, marking a substantial five percentage point improvement [E20]. Furthermore, focusing narrowly on short-term quarterly noise obscures the powerful compounding engine documented in the five-year record, where sales grew at a robust 16% annualized rate [E8]. This persistent top-line expansion drove profit growth of 14% over five years, vastly outpacing the stock's meager 6% price appreciation and directly validating the scanX signal engine's diagnosis that fundamentals are outpacing the stock and signaling potential undervaluation [E46]. Finally, dismissing the business on the basis of a zero dividend yield [E4] or modest near-term ROE and ROCE figures [E7, E6] disregards the reality that high-growth compounding phases naturally require capital reinvestment rather than immediate cash payouts.

Conceded: five-year sales compounded at 16% [E8], and five-year profit growth of 14% outpaced the 6% price rise [E46]. However, the bull's reliance on multi-year margin expansion to 14% [E20] is directly undercut by the most recent quarterly data showing operating margins contracting to 11% in March 2026, representing a severe three percentage point compression year-over-year [E21]. This sharp recent margin reversal exposes the fragility of relying on past structural gains while pricing in an aggressive 17.4% growth rate—far above the 14.0% base case—just to justify the current ₹ 244 share price [E37]. Furthermore, dismissing low returns is unconvincing when the fundamental returns themselves are mediocre, anchored by an uninspiring ROCE of 11.5% [E6] and a low ROE of 9.2% [E7]. Finally, zero dividend yield [E4] combined with a rich P/E of 37.8x [E1] means shareholders are paying a steep multiple for a business where intrinsic value sits deeply discounted at ₹ 190 [E35], leaving a negative margin of safety of -28.4% [E36].
